title: Colchicine as a Repurposed NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitor in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Mechanistic Rationale, Existing Clinical Evidence, and Proposal for a Precision Biomarker Trial
content: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterised by progressive motor neuron loss and neuroinflammation. Current disease-modifying therapies provide only marginal benefit, and microglial NLRP3 inflammasome hyperactivation has emerged as a key pathological amplifier common to all ALS genetic and sporadic subtypes. We hypothesise that low-dose colchicine can attenuate microglial NLRP3-driven neuroinflammation in ALS, thereby slowing motor neuron loss and disease progression. NLRP3 activation is documented across ALS subtypes including SOD1, C9orf72, and TDP-43 proteinopathies. Colchicine inhibits NLRP3 through tubulin disruption and ASC oligomerisation blockade, crosses the blood-brain barrier, and has established safety in long-term use. The Co-ALS randomised trial demonstrated acceptable safety in ALS patients. We propose a precision-medicine Phase 2b trial (COLCHICINE-ALS-PRECISION) stratifying patients by baseline plasma chitotriosidase-1 (CHIT1) — a validated microglial activation biomarker — to maximise the detectable treatment effect in the high-neuroinflammation subpopulation. High-CHIT1 patients are predicted to derive maximum benefit and should be prioritised for recruitment.
